## 1. Purpose / Scope

This Security Domain Review Input Addendum is designed to capture the security architecture and compliance posture for projects seeking security domain approval. The following concerns should be addressed in this document:

1. `Clearly define the security scope` and boundaries of the initiative including data classification and sensitivity
2. `Ensure regulatory alignment` with applicable compliance frameworks (HIPAA, NIST, SOC 2, FIPS 140, etc.)
3. `Identify security stakeholders` and their roles including the CISO, security architects, and compliance officers
4. `Provide security architecture overview` with threat model, control objectives, and defense-in-depth approach
5. `Assess security risks` with likelihood, impact ratings, and proposed mitigations
6. `Address identity and access management` requirements including authentication, authorization, and least privilege
7. `Evaluate data protection controls` covering encryption at rest, in transit, and key management strategy
8. `Consider vulnerability management` including secure SDLC practices, penetration testing, and patch cadence

## 3. Security Architecture Assessment

For each control below, provide a **Response** (Yes / No / N-A). A supporting comment is **required** for every response — briefly describe how the control is satisfied, why it does not apply, or what remediation is planned.

### 3.1 Network Security

| Control ID | Question | Response |
| ---------- | -------- | -------- |
| NET-001 | Are trust zones defined and enforced based on data classification; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| NET-002 | Are network boundaries enforced with deny-by-default, least-privilege filtering between zones? | |
| NET-003 | Is remote access through secure access services such as VPN with MFA; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| NET-005 | Are detection and prevention controls positioned at ingress, egress (NGFW, IDPS, WAF, ZTNA); described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| NET-007 | Is TLS 1.2+ or TLS 1.3 enforced for all in-transit traffic, including internal service-to-service communication and described in the ARB documents and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| NET-010 | Are network zones explicitly defined for DMZ, internal, restricted, and management planes; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| NET-011 | Are data flows described in the ARB documents and identified on the architecture diagram with uni-directional and bi-directional arrows? | |
| NET-012 | Are data flows identified and logs aggregated to the SIEM/SOAR; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| NET-013 | Are VLAN, subnet, VPC, or VNet segmentation; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| NET-014 | Are WAF, WAAP, and API gateway controls placed in front of public web and API endpoints; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |

### 3.5 AI Security

| Control ID | Question | Response |
| ---------- | -------- | -------- |
| AI-002 | Are trust boundaries explicitly defined between users, orchestration layers, models, vector stores, tools, and downstream systems; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AI-003 | Are defenses against direct and indirect prompt injection built into the application and orchestration design; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AI-004 | Are model outputs validated, sanitized, and policy-checked before they are rendered, stored, or executed downstream; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AI-005 | Are vector stores, embeddings, and RAG pipelines protected with access control, encryption, namespace isolation, and poisoning defenses; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AI-006 | Are high-risk AI decisions or autonomous actions required to have human approval or bounded human oversight; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AI-007 | Are privacy controls enforced for prompts, context, and outputs, including redaction, minimization, DLP; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AI-008 | Are controls in place against model inversion, membership inference, model extraction, and unauthorized model access; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AI-010 | Is AI supply-chain provenance tracked for models, datasets, embeddings, prompts, and supporting dependencies; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AI-012 | Are AI provider credentials, model endpoints, and agent secrets vaulted; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AI-013 | Are agentic workflows sandboxed; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AI-015 | Are MCP servers, plugins, or external tool connectors isolated; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AI-016 | Are input and output guardrails applied consistently across the full AI request path; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AI-017 | Are protections in place to prevent system-prompt leakage, training-data leakage, and sensitive context exfiltration in model responses; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AI-018 | Are model endpoints protected with authentication, quota controls, and abuse detection suitable for token-based denial-of-service; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AI-023 | Is there a technical kill switch or rapid-disable path for unsafe models, tools, or agent behaviors; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |

### 3.6 AI Gateway Security

| Control ID | Question | Response |
| ---------- | -------- | -------- |
| AIG-001 | Is an AI gateway or equivalent control plane used as the single egress path for enterprise LLM; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AIG-002 | Does the gateway enforce centralized authentication and authorization; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AIG-003 | Are provider API keys and tokens vaulted at the gateway; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AIG-004 | Does the gateway enforce token limits, rate limits, budget caps, and cost quotas; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AIG-005 | Are input guardrails such as prompt-injection detection, jailbreak filtering, and secret scanning applied; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AIG-007 | Is DLP or PII redaction enforced on both prompts and completions before data crosses the enterprise boundary; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AIG-008 | Is an approved-model allow-list enforced to block unsanctioned providers, models, or shadow AI usage; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AIG-009 | Does model routing, fallback, and load balancing preserve security policy consistently across all routes; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AIG-011 | Are prompt and response audit trails captured centrally with redaction, traceability, and retention controls; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AIG-013 | Are data residency and geo-routing controls enforced so prompts are sent only to compliant regions and providers; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AIG-014 | Are plugin, tool, or MCP invocations routed through the gateway allow-listed, authenticated, and policy-enforced; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AIG-016 | Does the gateway detect and flag abusive patterns such as jailbreak sweeps, scraping, token flooding, or mass prompt probing; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AIG-017 | Are content-type, payload-size, context-window, and max-token limits enforced at the gateway; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AIG-018 | Does the gateway integrate with SIEM or SOAR for real-time alerting; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| AIG-020 | Are high-availability, failover, and circuit-breaker patterns implemented; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |

### 3.7 Data Security

| DATA-001 | Is data classified and labeled in a way that drives technical controls throughout the architecture; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |

| DATA-004 | Is sensitive data encrypted in transit across all internal and external communication paths; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
| DATA-008 | Are DLP controls positioned across endpoint, email, cloud, and network egress channels for sensitive data classes; described in the ARB document and identified on the architecture diagram? | |
